abstract: The earliest stage of embryonic patterning replies on the regulation of maternal mRNA translation by RNA-binding proteins, such as Bicaudal-C (Bicc1). However, the molecular mode of action of Bicc1 in regulating translation remains unclear. In a new study, Charlotte R. Kanzler, Michael D. Sheets and colleagues show that a 300 amino acid long repression domain on the C-terminal end of Bicc1 is required in coordinating anterior-posterior patterning at earlier stages of Xenopus development but not in establishing left-right asymmetry at later stages. This reveals that Bicc1 uses developmental stage-specific molecular strategies to exert translational control. To learn more about this work and the people behind it, we spoke to first author Charlotte R. Kanzler and Michael (Mike) D. Sheets, Professor in the Department of Molecular Chemistry at University of Wisconsin-Madison, Wisconsin (USA).
